neighbours.label: contrastive 'but' (or comma) right after a statement that two things are alike: the turn from similarity to difference
fire: Lions and tigers are both large cats that hunt at night, but they live on different continents.
The two phones share the same processor and screen size, but one has a much better camera.
My sister and I have the same eye colour and height, but our personalities could not be more different.
Both recipes call for flour, sugar and butter, but the second one adds a pinch of cardamom.
The twins attended the same school and played the same sport, but they chose very different careers.
Crocodiles and alligators look almost identical at first glance, but their snouts have different shapes.
The two novels were written in the same decade and the same city, but their tone is completely unlike.
Both cars use the same engine and chassis, but the sports model has a stiffer suspension.
quiet: Lions and tigers are both large cats that hunt at night and they both rely on stealth.
The two phones share the same processor and screen size and even the same battery.
My sister and I have the same eye colour and height and we often wear similar clothes.
Both recipes call for flour, sugar and butter and both are baked for forty minutes.
The twins attended the same school and played the same sport throughout their childhood.
Crocodiles and alligators are reptiles that spend much of their time in warm water.
The two novels were written in the same decade and published by the same small house.
Both cars use the same engine and chassis and are built at the same factory.
